text: Willer Bordon (16 January 1949 – 14 July 2015) was an Italian academic, businessman, and politician who held various cabinet positions during the late 1990s and 2000s. He was born in Muggia, Province of Trieste, on 16 January 1949. Bordon served as mayor of Muggia for eleven years and was elected to the Italian parliament in 1987 as a deputy representing Trieste. In 1992, he founded the Democratic Alliance, a small centre-left party, but resigned from it in June 1994 after poor performance in the general election. He later joined the Margherita party. From 1998 to 1999, he served as minister for public works. In April 2000, he was appointed minister of environment in the cabinet led by Prime Minister Giuliano Amato, taking over the role from Edo Ronchi. Bordon also served as a member of the Italian Senate, retiring from the Senate in 2008. After leaving politics, he became president of Enalg SpA and began working as a professor of political science at La Sapienza University. Bordon died at the age of 66 on 14 July 2015.
